meta.title: Cadente — agents, terminal, database and notes in one window
meta.description: Cadente is a free desktop app that puts Claude Code, Codex, a terminal, an API client, a database client, notes and a calendar in one split window. Every part is a plugin: keep what you use and turn off the rest, even the AI. Built in Rust, for Mac, Windows and Linux.
meta.ogDescription: Agents, terminal, database and notes in one window. Every part is a plugin, and you only turn on what you use.

hero.eyebrow: Free · Mac, Windows and Linux · built in Rust
hero.lede: Put Claude Code and Codex to work side by side while you test the API, query the database and wrap up the meeting notes. All in the same window, all from the keyboard. Every piece is a plugin: keep what you use and turn off the rest, even the AI. And it costs nothing.
hero.earn: Build plugins and keep up to 90% of what they earn

theater.label: Cadente in use
theater.intro: A working day in Cadente, from 9 am to the end of the day

creator.title:
Your plugin
can become income.
creator.lede: Had an idea that fixes your day? It probably fixes other people's too. Describe it to the agent, it writes the plugin, you publish it in the store and choose how to charge. You keep 90% of donations and 70% of sales and of every subscription renewal.
creator.donationText: The plugin is free, and people who like it can support you.
creator.subscriptionText: Monthly or yearly. You earn on every renewal, not just the first.
creator.onceText: People pay once and use it on up to 5 computers.
creator.trialText: Let people try it for a few days before you charge.

calc.note: This is an estimate, before taxes and card fees. It is calculated on the net amount, and every sale goes through the Cadente checkout.

creator.makerTitle: From idea to store, without leaving Cadente.
creator.makerLede: Three example requests, each earning a different way: a pet Cadu loose on the screen, a dashboard with today's sales and a status page that tells you when GitHub, Cloudflare or AWS go down. You can drag Cadu around, feed him and give him a bath.
creator.step1Text: A Chat opens with the request. Nothing is sent until you press <kbd>↵</kbd>.
creator.step2Text: Manifest, code and tests, in a pane next to where you are.
creator.step3Text: cadente plugin dev runs the plugin right there, next to the conversation. Cadu lives loose on top of the app: drag him, press f to feed him and b for a bath.
creator.step4Text: /publish and that's it: it is in the store, at the price you chose.

rust.title:
Rust from the core
to the screen.
The fan never kicks in.
rust.lede: No hidden browser and no Node running behind it. Cadente is native, drawn by the GPU, and only uses energy when something changes on screen.
rust.stack: cadente ├─ core rust ├─ interface rust · slint, drawn by the GPU ├─ terminal rust · native pty ├─ agents rust · claude, codex, agy and any cli └─ plugins rust · webassembly for community ones
rust.memoryText: History stays on disk and only loads when you open it. The app does not grow over time.
rust.batteryText: Stopped typing? Cadente stops too and lets the processor rest.
rust.hiddenText: Close the pane and it is gone. No terminal, agent or plugin keeps running behind it.

plugins.eyebrow: 18 built-in plugins · millions from the community
plugins.title:
Every pane becomes
what you need.
plugins.lede: Chat, Terminal, PRs, Requests, Calendar, Focus: 18 plugins come with the app, and they all work the same way. <kbd>↵</kbd> opens, <kbd>.</kbd> shows what you can do, <kbd>/</kbd> lists the commands, <kbd>⇥</kbd> switches the view. Learn one and you know them all. Click one to see it.
plugins.communityText: Beyond the 18 built-in ones there is the store: anyone can publish plugins there, and they add up to millions. Installing is always free and takes one <kbd>↵</kbd>. Don't use AI? Keep only the productivity ones.

owner.title:
Your Cadente,
your rules.
owner.lede: The Chat, the Terminal, the sidebar, the AI provider, even the theme: everything is a plugin, just like the community ones. Don't like one? Turn it off, swap it or rip it out. It works without AI too: turn it off and keep a productivity hub with a terminal, database, notes, calendar and focus.
owner.installText: From the store, a link or a folder, without restarting anything.
owner.removeText: Any plugin can go, even the built-in ones.
owner.swapText: Before you swap the provider, you see what will change.
owner.noSurpriseText: You see the permissions before installing, and again if an update asks for more.

store.title:
Millions of plugins
one ↵ away.
store.lede: Kanban, Kubernetes, lo-fi radio, a board for diagrams: if someone needed it, someone built it. Cadente has no paid plan, installing costs nothing and most plugins are free.
store.empty: No plugin with that name yet. Why not build yours?
store.oneClickText: It downloads, checks the file is the right one, shows the permissions and installs.
store.openText: Published on GitHub with the cadente-plugin topic? Your plugin is in the store.
store.watchedText: If a malicious plugin shows up, it is blocked and turns itself off on every machine.

finale.title:
Ready to open
the first pane?
finale.lede: It's free, runs on Mac, Windows and Linux, and asks for no card.
